content.text: The pod's PVC is bound to a `local` PV pinned to the failed node (`nodeAffinity: kubernetes.io/hostname In [ip-10-0-7-21]`), so the scheduler reports "volume node affinity conflict" on every healthy node. The only ways forward either wait on the failed node or require destroying the PVC/PV (which has `reclaimPolicy: Delete` on a local disk, i.e. losing the Redis AOF buffer of unacknowledged settlements). That's a data-loss decision I shouldn't make unilaterally.

input.reason: ledger-queue-0 is pinned to failed node ip-10-0-7-21 by a local PersistentVolume (storageClass local-nvme, nodeAffinity kubernetes.io/hostname=ip-10-0-7-21, reclaimPolicy: Delete). Scheduler message confirms "volume node affinity conflict" on all 8 healthy nodes. Per docs, local volumes are tied to the underlying node's availability and the pod cannot run if that node is unhealthy; node affinity on a PV constrains scheduling to that node [cite: concepts/storage/volumes#local-0] [cite: concepts/storage/persistent-volumes#node-affinity-0]. Force-deleting the pod does not help because the StatefulSet retains the existing PVC after node failure and tries to reattach the same volume [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset#persistentvolumeclaim-retention-1]. Two possible fixes, both needing a human decision: (1) wait for infra to bring ip-10-0-7-21 back, preserving the AOF buffer; (2) accept data loss of in-flight settlements by deleting PVC data-ledger-queue-0 and the bound PV local-pv-ip-10-0-7-21-nvme1 (reclaimPolicy Delete will drop the on-disk AOF) so the StatefulSet can bind a new local-nvme PV on a healthy node. Option 2 risks losing unacknowledged settlement messages and must be chosen by the service owner / infra; please engage a human engineer before 15:00 cutoff.
